AUTHOR: Mathias
TITLE: Deep Neural Network Driven Automated Underwater Object Detection
REGION: Taiwan (F4K/LifeCLEF), Western Australia (UWA/OzFish), Bali (Bubble Vision), tropical Australia (DeepFish)
DATA: LifeCLEF 2015 (F4K); UWA dataset (OzFish, ref 19); Bubble Vision Bali videos; DeepFish
D2: UWA: ~2180 train / 1020 test frames; DeepFish: 30% validated and tested
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'Among these, around 2180 frames are used as training frames and 1020 frames are subjected to testing.'
R_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'The performance analysis is shown for the LCF-15 dataset, UWA dataset, Bubble Vision dataset and the DeepFish dataset in Fig. 7.' (each dataset evaluated separately)
C_EV: Sec. 3: 'The threshold is set to 0.4 in our experiments for appropriate box generation.'
E_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'The accuracy for fish identification is 98.5 percent, 96.77 percent, 97.99 percent and 95.3 percent respectively'
ARCH: DLIR diffraction-limited restoration + BEMD-adapted GMM with VGG16 transfer learning + YOLOv3, OR-fused
METR: Accuracy, precision, recall, IoU, average tracking error, detection FPS; PSNR/MSE/SSIM/EPI for restoration
NOTE: Included because UWA (OzFish) and DeepFish field datasets are evaluated; LifeCLEF is benchmark-only and Bubble Vision is web video. Training data per test dataset are not clearly described; R coded N assuming per-dataset train/test (no explicit cross-dataset test). D coded from UWA frame-count split (no grouping stated); DeepFish 30% portion appears to be the predefined split but unit not stated. Table 3 reports tracking error by scene type (blurred/occluded/dynamic/standard) - not coded as visibility stratification (blur is not a measured water condition); a verifier could argue V1=정성 서술만, V6=P. The 0.4 'threshold' is described as NMS/confidence threshold, choice reasoned only qualitatively.
